records.title: Carroll civil judgment for sexual abuse and defamation
records.summary: A federal civil jury found Trump liable for sexually abusing E. Jean Carroll and defaming her, awarding $5 million. The Second Circuit affirmed the judgment in December 2024.
records.sourceLabel: U.S. Courts opinion repository — Carroll v. Trump, No. 23-793
records.jurisdiction: Southern District of New York / Second Circuit, United States
records.status: civil judgment affirmed; Supreme Court rehearing petition pending as of last check
records.outcome: Civil liability judgment affirmed on appeal; Supreme Court denied certiorari on June 29, 2026, and a rehearing petition was distributed on July 23, 2026.
records.rightOfReply: Trump has denied Carroll's allegation and challenged the judgment through post-trial motions, appeal, and Supreme Court proceedings.
records.counterEvidence: This is a civil finding, not a criminal conviction. The current Supreme Court docket shows a rehearing petition remained pending at the last check.
records.proofNeeded: A Supreme Court rehearing disposition or later court order could change the final appellate posture.
records.boundary: This record must be described as a civil judgment. It does not support labeling Trump criminally convicted of a sexual offense.

records.title: Supreme Court review posture in Carroll case
records.summary: The Supreme Court docket records denial of certiorari on June 29, 2026, followed by a corrected petition for rehearing filed July 8 and distributed July 23, 2026.
records.sourceLabel: Supreme Court of the United States docket 25-573
records.jurisdiction: Supreme Court of the United States
records.status: rehearing petition pending at last check
records.outcome: Certiorari denied; rehearing request not yet resolved as of July 26, 2026.
records.rightOfReply: Trump's denial and legal challenges are preserved in the docket and underlying appellate proceedings.
records.counterEvidence: A pending rehearing petition means the Supreme Court posture should be updated when the Court acts.
records.proofNeeded: The final Supreme Court order on rehearing is required to close this review record.
records.boundary: This is a procedural-status record, not a new finding about the underlying conduct.
